Attempted live read-only queries against cluster `fixture-cluster` via the GKE MCP read-only API:
- `gke_get_k8s_resource` (Pod `drill-rbac-probe-d9d9f54f7-tpnjh`, Deployment `drill-rbac-probe`)

```

---

- **Execution Blocker:** The service account executing the subagent lacks the IAM permission `mcp.googleapis.com/tools.call` on the project `fixture-project` (or MCP API access is restricted). As a result, live cluster introspection (inspecting pod manifests, container logs, exit codes, and RBAC bindings) could not be completed directly against the cluster.

Given the workload name `drill-rbac-probe`, typical failure modes involve missing ServiceAccount RBAC permissions (e.g., trying to query Kubernetes API resources without appropriate Role/RoleBinding permissions or using the default service account).

---

#### 4. Remediation Steps & Proposed IAM Fix

   Grant the agent's caller identity permission to invoke the MCP endpoint (`mcp.googleapis.com/tools.call` or appropriate role) on project `fixture-project`.

   kubectl logs -n drill-target drill-rbac-probe-d9d9f54f7-tpnjh -c probe --previous

   ```
   If the probe requires API access (e.g. `get`/`list` on pods/deployments), ensure a dedicated `ServiceAccount`, `Role`, and `RoleBinding` are bound to `Deployment/drill-rbac-probe`.
